aggregates.claim: A finite ledger over the exact current collected suite, with every execution ID, primary requirement, input/profile fingerprint, current adjudication, declared phase and evidence class bound into the inventory review. Inventory adjudication is distinct from case approval: explicit current needs-oracle or disputed members remain listed, unapproved and ineligible for qualified passes. Unreviewed, stale or falsely labelled reference evidence cannot be silently adopted. Declared-valid runtime effects, other effects, positive admission controls, undefined-result contexts and invalid-input diagnostics have separate populations. Actual observations are joined by exact ID and compiler configuration without adding an execution or attributing a canonical case to this requirement.
aggregates.limitation: Observational infrastructure only: S4.2-001's facet remains pending until the source/requirement census, complete conforming fixture/oracle inventory and separate processor/dependency qualifications are independently established. No finite run proves the universal processor obligation. A filtered invocation retains all unselected members in its denominator. XFAILs remain failures; skips, unsupported modes, missing profiles, unavailable launchers, unexecuted run effects and provisional observations cannot become qualified passes. A compile/link admission is not execution of an interpretation, and a context-only run is not an assertion about an undefined value. Resource failures do not establish permitted size/complexity limits. Compiler headers, companions, launchers and profile observations describe the selected interface, not ABI certification or universal portability. Paragraphs 7-8 are recommendations, not manufactured mandatory documentation requirements.

review.rationale: Explicit source-context renewal of the unchanged 2083-member inventory after the independently reviewed 10.2.1.1, 10.2.1.2, 10.2.1.4 and 10.2.1.5 source registration in doc/source_audits/batch_106.json. All 2083 case bindings, their fingerprints, 2047 raw reviews, 209 older catalogues, 22 links, R402 and the b153c75b baseline remain exact. Only 12 of the 14 scoped base units are newly accounted, because R1033 and C1015 were already accounted; 89 new facets remain pending. The central question in this scope was the ownership boundary with 10.2.1.3, which was already registered and sits in the middle of the packet with 26 base units and 144 facets. The reviewer read that catalogue in full and checked both failure directions, finding neither duplication nor gap: the allocatable, character-kind and deferred-length cases are admission rules here, while the resulting allocation, length, bounds, truncation, padding, conversion and values remain owned by 10.2.1.3, and pointer association changes remain with 10.2.2. The zero-permissions verdict was independently adjudicated and accepted: the sentence permitting pure elemental subroutine assignments to be performed simultaneously or in any order occurs only in the unnumbered NOTE in 10.2.1.5 and is informative, while 10.2.1.3 out of scope carries genuine normative latitude at p4, p7 and p16 already recorded as permissions. Table 10.8 was read row by row from the table itself and all eight rows are owned, with the enum row preserving that when expr is integer a primary in expr shall be an enumerator of the enum type rather than an arbitrary integer. Character plans assert LEN explicitly rather than relying on blank-padded comparison, and no plan assumes that ISO 10646 or ASCII kinds exist. No intrinsic-assignment effect, defined-assignment execution, canonical link or SourceUse observation is supplied, and no compiler was invoked. The eight substring executions integrated in batch099 remain the latest actual observations. All pending facets, unresolved units, the retained needs-oracle real-BOZ block and every global gate remain open.
